candidates.title: From Sweep to Seam: Interleaved Cross-Block Post-Training Quantization
candidates.abstract: Compressing large language models to two bits or fewer is increasingly feasible through block-wise post-training quantization; cross-block variants reconstruct neighboring Transformer blocks within a moving window. In the fixed two-block setting studied here, the matched sequential baseline moves this window through the network once, so errors introduced early in the sweep are not revisited. We propose Interleaved Cross-Block Quantization (ICBQ), a scheduling modification that revisits the boundary pair between consecutive chunks. Each seam pair is refined twice: first at the end of one chunk and again at the start of the next. The method retains the local two-block objective and reuses the calibration inputs of existing block-wise PTQ pipelines. Under stated local contraction and smoothness assumptions, we derive a depth-wise upper-bound comparison in which seam revisits multiply the propagated term while the residual remains bounded independently of depth. In the reported experiments, ICBQ reduces ternary-quantization perplexity relative to the matched Sequential CBQ baseline, yields finite perplexity in configurations where the baseline has severe degradation, and can also be used with 3-bit and 2-bit GPTQ.
candidates.reason: ICBQは隣接Transformerブロックを一度だけ順次再構成する低ビットPTQの誤差伝播に対し、チャンク境界の二ブロック組を二度最適化する交互スケジュールを導入する。三値DBFと2・3ビットGPTQでLLM重み圧縮時のPPL劣化を評価する、推論用低ビット化に直結する技術であるためaccept。

candidates.title: Parser Transitions Already Reveal Structural Responsibility: KV Persistence for Structured Generation
candidates.abstract: LLM agents use structured generation for JSON, SQL, and function calls. Constrained decoding ensures valid formats, but KV compression can discard history needed for correct function and argument selection. Structural responsibility can diverge from model saliency: importance scores can overlook generated tokens'structural roles. Parser transitions already computed for legality encode these roles, including required arguments and structural boundaries, providing a free retention signal. We introduce PASK (Parser-Aware Structural KV Persistence), which reuses this signal for KV persistence by layer group without online importance estimation. Task-error sensitivity sets protection floors, while attention-output distortion ranks upgrades under the remaining budget. Offline calibration produces a frozen table for structural lookup and budget accounting. PASK outperforms budget-controlled baselines on function calling and text-to-SQL, improving BFCL accuracy by up to 8.67 pp over the strongest comparator. Against Full KV, it cuts peak GPU memory by 47.5 percent and achieves up to 3.3 times TPOT speedup.
candidates.reason: PASKはJSON・SQL・関数呼出しを制約付き復号するパーサ遷移から、必須フィールドや引数に関わるトークンの構造的責任を抽出する。オフラインでタスク誤り感度による保護下限と注意出力の歪みに基づく残余KV予算配分を学習し、オンラインでは構造別の保持表を参照する。KV圧縮による推論メモリ削減と構造化生成の正確性を直接扱うためaccept。worklistの旧タイトルとarXiv現行タイトルが異なるがarXiv IDで同定。

candidates.title: Quantization Error Is Spectrally Flat: A Single Random Probe Is a Calibrated, Data-Free Sensitivity Estimator, with Application to Budget-Targeted Mixed-Precision Quantization
candidates.abstract: A single random Gaussian probe gives an unbiased estimate of the squared Frobenius norm of a layer's quantization error. The estimator is well-behaved because round-to-nearest error is spectrally flat. Across 1,683 tensors from a 35B MoE and a 9B dense model, effective dimensionality is 0.93 to 0.96 times the i.i.d. noise value of the same shape, and on the MoE the median is unchanged from 2-bit to 8-bit. The probe coefficient of variation is predictable from tensor shape. One probe measures per-tensor sensitivity to within 4 to 7%; twenty probes reach 1.3 to 1.4%.RAM applies the propagated form of this estimator to budget-targeted mixed-precision quantization with no calibration data. Gaussian probes carrying the network's own input statistics score every tensor at six bit-widths. A knapsack solver allocates bits under an exact byte budget, with guardrails against catastrophic 2-bit assignments. One probe pass serves any budget. Isolated and propagated scores rank tensors independently on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (Spearman -0.01), yet the propagated probe rank-correlates 0.81 to 0.83 with the GPTQ layer objective from real activations, while the isolated estimator is uncorrelated with it. That objective is the wrong allocation target: at matched bytes on Qwen3.8-27B, a block-output probe beats a vendor IQ3_M mix and an oracle that allocates from the real-activation objective. On Qwen3-8B the propagated probe ties HAWQ-V2 at matched bytes. Across seven architectures from 8B to 122B, with probe timing up to a 400B model in nine minutes on one workstation, RAM reaches 3.5 to 13.6% lower median WikiText-2 perplexity than size-comparable uniform 4-bit builds on the tested MoE models. (Black Sheep Ai baa.ai)
candidates.reason: 量子化誤差のFrobeniusノルムをガウス乱数プローブで推定し、RAMが層間伝播を含む感度を較正データなしで求め、ナップサック問題としてLLM各テンソルのビット幅をバイト予算へ配分する。MoEと密モデルの低ビット重み推論を対象とした混合精度量子化手法なのでaccept。

candidates.title: JetSpec++: Foresight Parallel Drafting with Self Refinements
candidates.abstract: Speculative decoding's effectiveness is governed by two quantities: the acceptance rate of drafted tokens and the cost of producing them. We show the two objectives can be co-optimized with algorithm-system co-design, and present JetSpec++, which retains a strong learned draft model while hiding its cost almost entirely. JetSpec++ combines three components: intra-block self refinement, which trains the draft model to iteratively correct its own parallel predictions within a block of tokens; inter-block foresight drafting, which begins the next block before the current one is verified; and pipelined drafting and verification, which overlaps the two stages so drafting's marginal wall-clock cost approaches zero. In comparison with state-of-the-art speculative decoding methods, JetSpec++ attains a wall-clock speedup of up to $7.45\times$ over autoregressive (AR) decoding and $1.54\times$ over DSpark, with up to 1,361 tokens per second for a single request on GB200, and an average acceptance length of 8.94 across seven benchmarks, while preserving the target model's output distribution. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/JetSpec.
candidates.reason: JetSpec++はドラフトのブロック内自己修正、現ブロックの検証完了前に次ブロックを予測する先行ドラフト、ドラフト・検証のパイプライン重畳を組み合わせる。対象LLMの出力分布を保ちつつ投機的復号の直列待ちを減らす直接的な推論高速化なのでaccept。
